importantNotes: 1 Corinthians 13 (the love chapter) is one of the most read passages at weddings.
Chapter 15 is the most detailed teaching on the resurrection in the Bible.
Paul's teaching on the Lord's Supper (ch. 11) is the earliest written account.
The body of Christ metaphor (ch. 12) teaches that every believer has a vital role.
Corinth was one of the most morally corrupt cities in the ancient world.

chapters.1: Divisions in the church; the wisdom of the cross vs. worldly wisdom.
chapters.2: Paul came with the Spirit's power, not eloquence; God's wisdom revealed by the Spirit.
chapters.3: The Corinthians are still spiritual infants; the church is God's temple; leaders are servants.
chapters.4: Apostles as servants of Christ; Paul's hardships; a father's appeal.
chapters.5: A case of sexual immorality must be dealt with; expel the immoral brother.
chapters.6: Lawsuits among believers; the body is a temple of the Holy Spirit — flee immorality.
chapters.7: Teaching on marriage, singleness, and the principle of remaining in one's calling.
chapters.8: Food offered to idols; knowledge puffs up, but love builds up; consider the weak.
chapters.9: Paul's rights as an apostle; he gives up his rights for the gospel; run to win.
chapters.10: Warnings from Israel's history; flee idolatry; do everything for God's glory.
chapters.11: Head coverings in worship; proper observance of the Lord's Supper.
chapters.12: Spiritual gifts — one body, many parts; every member is necessary.
chapters.13: The love chapter — love is patient, kind, never fails; the greatest is love.
chapters.14: Prophecy is greater than tongues; orderly worship; everything done decently.
chapters.15: The resurrection of Christ and of believers — death is swallowed up in victory.
chapters.16: The collection for Jerusalem; final instructions, greetings, and encouragement.
